title: Nubra Valley & Diskit Monastery Travel Guide, Best Time, Routes, Attractions & Stay Tips
content:
Nubra Valley & Diskit Monastery, 

Nubra Valley is one of the most fascinating and unique landscapes in India. Located around 120 km north of Leh, this valley sits at an altitude of 10,000 feet (3,048 meters) - yet it feels like a desert dreamland surrounded by snow-clad peaks.

Known as the “Orchard of Ladakh” or the “Valley of Flowers,” Nubra is blessed with lush green villages, apricot orchards, and vast stretches of sand dunes that glow golden under the Himalayan sun. The contrasting scenery - green oases amidst arid mountains and silver rivers - makes Nubra one of the most photogenic destinations in Ladakh.

The valley’s most famous landmark is the Diskit Monastery, the largest and oldest monastery in Nubra. Overlooking the valley from a rocky hilltop, it houses a majestic 32-meter-tall statue of Maitreya Buddha that gazes serenely toward the Shyok River. The monastery exudes an ancient charm, offering not just a spiritual experience but also panoramic views of the valley and the surrounding mountains.

Nubra Valley lies beyond the Khardung La Pass (17,982 feet) - one of the highest motorable passes in the world. The journey from Leh to Nubra is itself a highlight, offering jaw-dropping Himalayan vistas, prayer-flag-draped mountain roads, and the thrilling adventure of crossing this legendary pass.

What makes Nubra truly special is its diverse geography and culture. The valley is formed by the confluence of the Shyok and Nubra Rivers, creating a fertile land where villages like Diskit, Hunder, Turtuk, and Sumur flourish with greenery, despite the high altitude.

From riding Bactrian (double-humped) camels in Hunder’s cold desert to exploring ancient monasteries, warm-hearted homestays, and quiet trails by the Shyok River, Nubra offers a perfect blend of adventure, peace, and local life.

Whether you’re a biker chasing high passes, a photographer capturing Ladakh’s contrasts, or a traveler seeking serenity, Nubra Valley and Diskit Monastery will leave an imprint on your soul.

Best Time to Visit Nubra Valley:

The best time to visit Nubra Valley is between May and September, when Khardung La Pass is open and the weather is pleasant.

  • May - June: Clear skies, blooming orchards, and comfortable temperatures.
  • July - August: Peak tourist season - ideal for camping and camel safaris.
  • September: Fewer crowds, perfect for photography with golden landscapes.
  • October - April: Harsh winters, limited accessibility due to snow at Khardung La.

How to Reach Nubra Valley:

Distance from Leh: 120 km (takes around 5 - 6 hours by road).

Route:
Leh - South Pullu - Khardung La - North Pullu - Khalsar - Diskit - Hunder

The drive from Leh to Nubra Valley via Khardung La Pass is an unforgettable experience. Roads are generally well maintained but can be steep and narrow in parts. Shared taxis and private cabs are available from Leh.

Other access points:

  • From Pangong Tso: via Shyok route (165 km, around 7 - 8 hours).
  • From Turtuk: 80 km drive along the Shyok River.

Permits for Nubra Valley:

All visitors require Inner Line Permits (ILP) to enter Nubra Valley since it’s close to the Indo-China border.

  • Indian citizens: ILP (available online or in Leh).
  • Foreign nationals: Protected Area Permit (PAP).

Always carry multiple copies of the permit for security checkpoints.

Top Attractions in Nubra Valley:

1- Diskit Monastery: The largest monastery in Nubra, home to the famous 32-meter Maitreya Buddha statue. Don’t miss the morning prayers for a serene spiritual experience.

2- Hunder Sand Dunes: Ride the rare double-humped Bactrian camels and enjoy a cold desert sunset.

3- Turtuk Village: A charming Balti village near the Line of Control - known for apricots, hospitality, and unique culture.

4- Sumur & Panamik: Known for hot springs and traditional Ladakhi life.

5- Khardung La Pass: Adventure begins here - one of the world’s highest motorable passes (17,982 ft).

Where to Stay in Nubra Valley:

Accommodation ranges from luxury camps to traditional Ladakhi homestays and budget guesthouses.

  • Hunder: Ideal for sand dunes and camel safaris.
  • Diskit: Central location, perfect for monastery visits.
  • Turtuk: Great for offbeat travelers.

Book in advance during summer as Nubra is one of the most visited valleys in Ladakh.

Things to Do in Nubra Valley:

  • Take a camel safari on the sand dunes of Hunder.
  • Visit Diskit Monastery and climb to the Maitreya Buddha viewpoint.
  • Explore local villages like Sumur and Turtuk for cultural immersion.
  • Try Ladakhi cuisine — momos, thukpa, butter tea.
  • Enjoy stargazing in the clear Himalayan night sky.

Essential Travel Tips Leh Ladakh Trip:

  • Acclimatize in Leh for at least 2 days before heading to Nubra.
  • Carry cash - limited ATMs beyond Leh.
  • Pack warm clothes, even in summer.
  • Mobile network: BSNL postpaid may work in parts; others have no signal.
  • Respect local customs and avoid littering in monasteries or dunes.
